mainTopic: Intention in blowing שופר, the order and length of the blasts, and their sources in the פסוקים
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an answer about children: we teach a קטן to blow שופר once he has reached חינוך, but before that we just do not stop him. Next the גמרא reads the משנה's rules about a מתעסק. It tries to prove רבא's ruling that blowing לשיר counts, and to challenge רבי זירא, who wanted the blower to have him in mind. Both attempts are pushed away, because the משנה's wording does not force those readings. Then a new משנה lays out the order of the blasts (three sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה) and how long each sound must be. It also covers someone who got a שופר only after the ברכות, and a dispute about whether the שליח ציבור covers everyone. אביי settles one clash with a ברייתא about the length of a תקיעה, but admits a real מחלוקת about whether a תרועה is moaning (שברים) or whimpering (יבבות). Finally, a ברייתא uses the פסוק about the יובל to teach that we blow with a שופר, with a plain תקיעה before and after each תרועה. The words 'in the seventh month' apply all of this to ראש השנה.

steps.title: Two teachings about children: trained age versus untrained age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes resolving two teachings about children blowing שופר. One teaching is about a קטן who has reached חינוך, and the other is about a קטן who has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about a child who has reached the age of training. Here, it is talking about a child who has not reached the age of training.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of an answer that started on the previous עמוד. It settles two teachings about children and the שופר by saying they are talking about children of different ages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two teachings seemed to treat children differently. The answer is that the difference depends on whether the child has reached חינוך. Once he has, we actively teach him the מצוה. Before that, we just do not stop him.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child below the age of בר מצוה
Has reached the age of training in מצוות
Here, meaning in this teaching (used to split two cases apart)

phrases.english: [That teaching is] about a minor who has reached the age of training;
here, [it is] about a minor who has not reached the age of training.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each teaching is about a different kind of child
steps.terutzMaskana: Whether we teach a child to blow depends on whether he has reached חינוך

steps.title: The משנה on the מתעסק, and what it seems to imply about blowing for music
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a מתעסק does not fulfill the מצוה. It reads into it that someone who blows לשיר does fulfill it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who blows without meaning to has not fulfilled his obligation. That implies that one who blows to make music has fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new line from the משנה and reads into it what it seems to leave out. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא tries to use that reading as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is someone who is not even trying to blow a proper שופר sound. Blowing לשיר is different: the person means to make the sound, just not for the מצוה. Since the משנה only rules out the מתעסק, it seems that blowing לשיר is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts without intention, unaware of what he is doing
He has fulfilled his obligation
This implies (introduces a reading into the text)
For music, for the sake of the song

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the מתעסק with the one blowing לשיר. The מתעסק is not even trying to blow a proper sound. The one blowing לשיר wants the sound, just not for the מצוה.

phrases.english: And one who acts unawares has not fulfilled [his obligation].
This implies: one who blows for music has fulfilled [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמִּתְעַסֵּק לֹא יָצָא הָא תּוֹקֵעַ לָשִׁיר יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: moves to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מתעסק does not fulfill the מצוה; by inference, one who blows לשיר does

steps.title: Does the משנה support רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this reading of the משנה supports רבא, who ruled that one who blows לשיר fulfills the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רבא, since רבא said: one who blows for music has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the reading from the last step as proof for רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a מצוה done without specific intention for the מצוה still counts. If the משנה really implies that blowing לשיר counts, then a משנה backs up רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (offers a suggestion that may be rejected)
Supports him
An אמורא who holds that one who blows לשיר fulfills the מצוה

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rava?
For Rava said:
One who blows for music has fulfilled [his obligation].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading from step 2 as proof
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that one who blows לשיר fulfills the מצוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reading of the משנה: only the מתעסק fails, so one who blows לשיר succeeds

steps.title: Maybe blowing for music also counts as מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps the משנה's word מתעסק also covers someone who blows לשיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe one who blows for music is also called a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof for רבא by suggesting a broader meaning for the word מתעסק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if מתעסק means just someone who is not trying to make a sound. If the משנה uses מתעסק for anyone without intention for the מצוה, then blowing לשיר is included and fails too. So the משנה does not prove רבא right. It just does not decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (introduces a pushback)
Also
Calls him, refers to him as

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the מתעסק does not prove רבא, because מתעסק might include one who blows לשיר.

phrases.english: Perhaps one who blows for music
is also called [by the משנה] one who acts unawares.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא תּוֹקֵעַ לָשִׁיר נָמֵי מִתְעַסֵּק קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבא's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a narrow meaning of מתעסק; it could be broader

steps.title: Hearing from a מתעסק, and what it implies about one blowing for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that hearing from a מתעסק does not count. It reads into it that hearing from someone who blows only for himself does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who hears from a מתעסק has not fulfilled his obligation. But one who hears from someone blowing for himself, what is the law? He has fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and draws out what it seems to imply. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the focus moves from the blower's own intention to whether he must have the listener in mind. Someone blowing for himself does mean to do the מצוה, but not for others. Since the משנה only rules out the מתעסק, it seems the listener is fine even if the blower did not have him in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hears
One who blows (sounds) for himself only
What [is the law]?

phrases.english: And one who hears from one who acts unawares has not fulfilled [his obligation].

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִן הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ לְעַצְמוֹ, מַאי?
phrases.english: But one who hears from one who sounds [the שופר] for himself, what [is the law]?
He has fulfilled [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִן הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ לְעַצְמוֹ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel move on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing from a מתעסק does not count; by inference, hearing from one who blows for himself does

steps.title: A challenge to רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests this reading refutes רבי זירא, who told his attendant to have him in mind while blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this refutes רבי זירא, since רבי זירא told his attendant: Have intention [for me] and blow for me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the reading from the last step to challenge רבי זירא's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's instruction shows he held that the blower must intend to make the listener fulfill the מצוה. If the משנה implies that hearing from someone blowing only for himself counts, then that intention is not needed. That goes against רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be a refutation of him
An אמורא who required the blower to have the listener in mind
His attendant
Have intention, focus your intention

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rabbi Zeira?
For Rabbi Zeira said to his attendant:
Have intention and blow for me!
phrases.notes: He means: have me in mind, so that I fulfill the מצוה through your blowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading from step 5 to attack רבי זירא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's view that the blower must intend to make the listener fulfill the מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that hearing from someone blowing only for himself counts, so the listener does not need to be in the blower's mind

steps.title: The משנה just repeated the word מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The משנה said מתעסק in the second clause only because it used that word in the first clause, so nothing can be read into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, since the first part taught about a מתעסק, the last part also taught about a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא by showing that the משנה's wording does not carry the meaning the challenge assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the משנה chose the word מתעסק on purpose, to exclude other cases. The answer is that the משנה simply kept the same word as its רישא for a matching style. So no inference can be made about someone blowing for himself, and רבי זירא is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (it was already mentioned)
The first clause
The latter clause
Taught

steps.whatToRemember: Both inferences from this משנה fall away. The משנה cannot prove רבא right or refute רבי זירא, because the word מתעסק might be broad, or might just be repeated for style.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא, תְּנָא סֵיפָא comes up again and again in the גמרא. It warns that a word in a later clause may just copy the earlier clause, so we cannot read into it.

phrases.english: Perhaps, since the first clause taught [about] one who acts unawares,
the latter clause also taught [about] one who acts unawares.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא מִתְעַסֵּק תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי מִתְעַסֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Removes the challenge against רבי זירא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge read meaning into a word the משנה may have used only to match the רישא

steps.title: The order and length of the שופר blasts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that there are three sets of three blasts each. It says a תקיעה is as long as three תרועות, and a תרועה is as long as three יבבות. One stretched-out תקיעה cannot count for two sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: The order of blasts is three sets of three. A תקיעה is as long as three תרועות, and a תרועה is as long as three short whimper-sounds. If someone blew the first תקיעה and then stretched the second one to the length of two, it only counts as one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out the basic order of the שופר blasts and how long each sound must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each set is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and this is done three times. The last case is someone who tries to save a blast by stretching the closing תקיעה of one set so it also opens the next set. The משנה says this does not work: it counts only once, so he must blow a new תקיעה to start the next set.

keyTerms.meaning: A long, straight שופר blast
A broken שופר sound made of short pieces
Short whimper-like sounds; three of them make up one תרועה
The required length or amount
Short for מתניתין, meaning 'our משנה'

phrases.english: MISHNA: The order of the blasts:
is three sets of three blasts each.
phrases.notes: Each set of three is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.

phrases.english: The length of a tekia is like three teruot,
the length of a terua is like three whimpers.
If he blew the first tekia
and stretched the second one to the length of two,
phrases.notes: He wants that one long blast to end the first set and also start the second set.

phrases.english: he has in his hand only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving on from the discussion about a מתעסק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה are required. A תקיעה equals three תרועות and a תרועה equals three יבבות. One stretched blast counts only once.

steps.title: Getting a שופר only after the ברכות
steps.stepSummary: Someone who already said the ברכות and only then got a שופר still blows all three full sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone already said the ברכות and only afterward got a שופר, he blows תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second rule. It covers a person who had no שופר while saying the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the blasts go together with the ברכות of מוסף. The משנה teaches that missing that timing does not cancel the מצוה. He still blows the complete order of three sets afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: He recited the ברכות (here, of מוסף)
It became available to him
Blows a תרועה

phrases.english: One who recited the blessings
phrases.notes: He means the ברכות of the מוסף prayer.

phrases.english: and afterward a shofar became available to him
blows a tekia, a terua, and a tekia, three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁבֵּירַךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַנָּה לוֹ שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new case about blowing after the ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who got a שופר after the ברכות still blows the full three sets.

steps.title: Must each individual pray, or does the prayer leader cover everyone
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says every individual is obligated just like the שליח ציבור. רבן גמליאל says the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the prayer leader is obligated, so is every single individual. רבן גמליאל says the prayer leader fulfills the obligation for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a dispute about the ראש השנה prayers. The question is whether each person must say them himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the obligation rests on each person, the same as on the שליח ציבור. רבן גמליאל disagrees: the שליח ציבור's prayer counts for the whole group, so individuals are covered by him.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader who prays on behalf of the community
An individual person
Fulfills their obligation for them
The תנא who disagrees with the first opinion here

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: (1) the order and length of the blasts, (2) blowing after the ברכות, and (3) the dispute over whether the שליח ציבור covers everyone.

phrases.english: Just as the prayer leader is obligated,
so too each and every individual is obligated.
Rabban Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: The prayer leader fulfills the obligation on behalf of the many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the same משנה, a dispute about the prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says each individual must pray. רבן גמליאל says the שליח ציבור covers the many.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives a different length for a תקיעה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה from a ברייתא that says a תקיעה is only as long as one תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the length of a תקיעה is like a תרועה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and immediately raises a contradiction. The משנה said a תקיעה equals three תרועות, but a ברייתא says it equals one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about the first part of the משנה. If a תקיעה must be as long as three תרועות, the ברייתא's shorter length would not be enough. Both sources cannot be giving the same law, so the גמרא needs to explain them.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Like a תרועה, meaning the same length as one תרועה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא wants a shorter blast than the משנה. אביי is about to show that they actually agree.

phrases.english: GEMARA: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The length of a tekia is like a terua!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first part of the משנה from step 8 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a תקיעה equals three תרועות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a תקיעה equals one תרועה, which contradicts the משנה's length.

steps.title: אביי: the two sources count differently
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה counts the תקיעות and תרועות of all three sets together, while the ברייתא counts just one set. So both mean that one תקיעה equals one תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Our תנא counts the תקיעה of all the sets and the תרועות of all the sets. The ברייתא's תנא counts just one set and no more.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He shows that the משנה and the ברייתא agree and only count in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three sets, so there are three תרועות in total. When the משנה says 'a תקיעה is like three תרועות', it is looking at all three sets together: the three תקיעות match the three תרועות. The ברייתא looks at one set, so it says one תקיעה matches one תרועה. The actual length is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
The outside תנא, meaning the author of the ברייתא
Sets or groups (here, sets of blasts)
And no more

steps.whatToRemember: There is no argument: a single תקיעה is as long as a single תרועה. The משנה's 'three תרועות' just means counting all three sets together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical length of a תקיעה: one תקיעה is as long as one תרועה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Our tanna is counting
the tekia of all the sets
and the teruot of all the sets.
phrases.notes: So he is matching three תקיעות against three תרועות, which means one each.

phrases.english: The tanna of the baraita is counting
one set and no more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תַּנָּא דִּידַן קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation showing both sources count differently but agree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires a תקיעה three times as long as a תרועה, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts all three sets together, and the ברייתא counts one set. Both mean one תקיעה equals one תרועה.

steps.title: Is a תרועה three whimpers or three broken blasts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a תרועה is as long as three יבבות, and challenges it from a ברייתא that says it is as long as three שברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a תרועה is as long as three whimpers. But a ברייתא teaches that a תרועה is as long as three broken blasts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and attacks it with a ברייתא that gives a different measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבבות are short whimper-like sounds, while שברים are longer, broken, moaning sounds. If the ברייתא measures a תרועה by three שברים, it seems to describe a longer and different kind of sound than the משנה does.

keyTerms.meaning: Whimpers: very short, quick sounds
Broken blasts: longer, moaning sounds
But isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? A standard way to open a challenge

phrases.english: The length of a teruah is like three whimpers.
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The length of a teruah is like three broken blasts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the length of a תקיעה was settled in steps 11 and 12, the גמרא now moves to the length of a תרועה from the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a תרועה equals three יבבות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא measures the תרועה by three שברים, which are a different and longer sound than יבבות.

steps.title: אביי: the two sources truly disagree about what a תרועה sounds like
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that here the תנאים really do disagree. The תרגום calls a תרועה a 'יבבא', which is the word used for סיסרא's mother's crying. One side holds she moaned (שברים), and the other holds she whimpered (יבבות).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Here they certainly disagree. The פסוק says 'a day of תרועה it shall be to you,' and the תרגום translates it as 'a day of יבבא.' About סיסרא's mother it says 'she wailed (ותיבב).' One master holds she let out long moans, and the other holds she let out short whimpers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by admitting that the משנה and the ברייתא hold different opinions, and he explains where their disagreement comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, אביי settled the earlier clash by showing both sources meant the same thing. Here he cannot do that, so he grounds a real מחלוקת in the פסוקים. Both sides agree that a תרועה is a 'יבבא' like the crying of סיסרא's mother. They disagree on whether her crying was long moaning (like שברים) or short whimpering (like יבבות).

keyTerms.meaning: They certainly disagree
We translate it (in the Aramaic תַּרְגּוּם)
She moaned long, sighing moans (like שברים)
She wailed in short whimpers (like יבבות)
The enemy general; his mother cried waiting for him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the answer in step 12. There אביי showed the sources really agree. Here he admits they truly disagree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת about what a תרועה sounds like is the background for blowing both שברים and תרועה, since there is doubt about which sound the תורה means.

phrases.english: Abaye said: In this, they certainly disagree,
as it is written: 'A day of teruah it shall be to you,'
and we translate: 'A day of yevava it shall be to you.'
And it is written about the mother of Sisera:
'Through the window she looked out
and the mother of Sisera wailed.'
One master holds she moaned long moans.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's view: the sound is like the longer שברים.

phrases.english: And one master holds she wailed short whimpers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admitting a real מחלוקת between תנאים and explaining its source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the משנה and ברייתא should agree, so the different measurement looked like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: They truly disagree. Both read 'תרועה' as the crying of סיסרא's mother, but one hears it as moaning (שברים) and the other as whimpering (יבבות).

steps.title: The source that the blowing must be with a שופר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how we know the blowing must be with a שופר, and answers from the פסוק 'והעברת שופר תרועה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How do we know the blowing must be with a שופר? The פסוק says: 'You shall sound the שופר of תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives the source for using a שופר specifically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the שופר directly, so we learn the תרועה must come from a שופר and not some other instrument. This פסוק is about יום כיפור of the יובל year, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
From where do we know?
The פסוק says (introduces the source)
You shall sound (proclaim)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that it is with a shofar?
The verse says:
'You shall sound the shofar of teruah.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9. This פסוק is about יום כיפור of the יובל year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: after the shape of the sounds, the גמרא now looks at which instrument must be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרועה must be blown with a שופר, as the פסוק about the יובל says 'שופר תרועה.'

steps.title: But how do we know this for ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that the פסוק only speaks about the יובל, and asks how we know a שופר is needed on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only teaches me about the יובל. How do I know it for ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that its proof covers only the יובל, and sets up the next move by asking about ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in step 15 is talking about יום כיפור of the יובל year. That does not automatically tell us what instrument to use on ראש השנה, so a second source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (this case); the source covers only this
The Jubilee, every fiftieth year

phrases.english: I only have this for the Jubilee,
from where do we know it for Rosh Hashanah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹבֵל, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the source in step 15 is limited to the יובל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that ראש השנה also requires a שופר.

steps.title: All the blasts of the seventh month must be alike
steps.stepSummary: The words 'in the seventh month' are not needed, because the פסוק already says יום הכפורים. So they teach that all the blasts of the seventh month, including ראש השנה, must be like each other, meaning with a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'in the seventh month.' It didn't need to say that, so why does it? To teach that all the blasts of the seventh month must be like one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by learning from extra words in the פסוק that ראש השנה, which is also in the seventh month, needs a שופר too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק already says 'on the Day of Atonement,' we already know which month it means, so 'in the seventh month' is extra. Extra words come to teach something: every תרועה in that month, both ראש השנה and יום כיפור of the יובל, must be the same, with a שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: In the seventh month (תִּשְׁרֵי)
The פסוק didn't need to say it, a sign of extra words
This one like that one; the same

steps.whatToRemember: A תרועה must be blown with a שופר. We learn this from the יובל, and the extra words 'in the seventh month' make every blast of that month alike, so ראש השנה needs a שופר too.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'in the seventh month,'
for the verse did not need to say 'in the seventh month,'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק already says 'on the Day of Atonement,' so we already know which month it is.

phrases.english: so why does the verse say 'in the seventh month'?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כׇּל תְּרוּעוֹת שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ שְׁבִיעִי
phrases.english: So that all the blasts of the seventh month
should be like one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'in the seventh month' teach that all the blasts of תשרי are alike, so ראש השנה also requires a שופר.

steps.title: A plain blast must come before the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word order 'שופר תרועה' that a plain blast (תקיעה) comes before the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know there is a plain blast before the תרועה? Because the פסוק says 'והעברת שופר תרועה': first 'שופר', then 'תרועה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how we know a plain, straight blast must come before the תרועה, and it answers from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word 'שופר' comes before the word 'תרועה'. The ברייתא reads 'שופר' alone as a plain blast, a תקיעה. So the order of the words teaches the order of the sounds: first a תקיעה, then the תרועה.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'straight' or plain blast, meaning a תקיעה
The long, plain, unbroken שופר sound
Before it, meaning before the תרועה
'The פסוק teaches', used to bring a source

steps.confusionAlert: 'פשוטה' does not mean 'simple' in the sense of easy. It means a straight, unbroken sound, the תקיעה, as opposed to the broken sound of a תרועה.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a straight blast comes before it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the תרועה. A 'straight blast' is a plain תקיעה.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'Then you shall sound the shofar, the teruah.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9. 'שופר' comes before 'תרועה' in the פסוק, so the plain blast comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's reading of the same פסוק from step 15, now moving from 'a שופר is needed' to the order of the blasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תקיעה must come before every תרועה, learned from the word order 'שופר תרועה'.

steps.title: A plain blast must come after the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'תעבירו שופר', which comes later in the פסוק, that a plain blast comes after the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know there is a plain blast after the תרועה? Because later in the same פסוק it says 'תעבירו שופר', another plain 'שופר' after the תרועה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא asks how we know a plain blast must also come after the תרועה, and answers from a later part of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the word 'תרועה', the פסוק says 'שופר' again: 'תעבירו שופר'. This second plain 'שופר' teaches a second תקיעה that follows the תרועה. Together with step 18, the pattern is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: After it, meaning after the תרועה
'You shall sound the שופר', the later words of the same פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Each תרועה is wrapped by a plain תקיעה on both sides: תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a straight blast comes after it?
The verse teaches: 'You shall sound the shofar.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 25:9. These words come after 'תרועה', so a plain blast follows it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 18. Step 18 covered the blast before the תרועה, and this covers the blast after it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תקיעה must come after every תרועה, learned from 'תעבירו שופר'.

steps.title: How do we know this applies on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that these פסוקים speak only about יובל, and asks how we know the תקיעה before and after applies on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know this about the יובל. How do I know it applies on ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices a gap: everything so far came from a פסוק about the יובל. It is setting up the next step by asking where we learn the same rule for ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source in steps 18 and 19 was about יום הכפורים of the יובל year, not about ראש השנה. So the ברייתא needs a separate reason to say that the תקיעה before and after the תרועה is also needed on ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have', meaning so far I have only learned this case
The fiftieth year, announced with שופר on יום הכפורים
The new year, the first of the seventh month

phrases.english: And I have this only for the Jubilee year;
phrases.notes: He means the תקיעה before and after the תרועה that we just learned.

phrases.english: on Rosh Hashanah, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹבֵל, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to extend the rule from steps 18 and 19 beyond יובל, the same kind of question as step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the תקיעה before and after the תרועה is also required on ראש השנה.

steps.title: The words 'in the seventh month' include ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words 'בחדש השביעי', which tie ראש השנה to the יובל blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'in the seventh month', so this applies on ראש השנה as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question of step 20 with the words 'in the seventh month' from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as in step 17, the words 'בחדש השביעי' link all the blowing of the seventh month together. ראש השנה is also in the seventh month, so it follows the same pattern of a תקיעה before and after each תרועה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the seventh month', the month of both ראש השנה and יום הכפורים

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה comes from the יובל פסוק, and 'in the seventh month' applies it to ראש השנה too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the basic pattern of the שופר blowing we do on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'In the seventh month.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק again. This uses the same idea as step 17: everything blown in the seventh month follows one pattern.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20, using the same words that step 17 used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'בחדש השביעי' connect ראש השנה to the יובל, so the תקיעה before and after the תרועה applies on ראש השנה too.
